speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The Jurong Town Corporation (Amendment) Bill 2017 comprises three sets of amendments to the Jurong Town Corporation Act.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: This will make it more convenient and faster for industrialists as they will only need to approach one agency for their business space needs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Industrialists will also receive better support for their land and space needs across the different stages of their growth because JTC will be able to better match their needs across all the public industrial land and space in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: This includes JTC's customised industrial facilities, which offer shared infrastructure and services to help industrialists reduce their setting-up and operating costs.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: After the consolidation, the Government would be able to undertake more holistic master-planning of industrial estates across Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We can also better easily identify opportunities for the sharing of infrastructure and amenities across adjacent estates.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: In addition, the pooling of industrial master-planning and infrastructure expertise under one agency improves public sector capabilities and operational efficiency.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Our focus is on ensuring a smooth transition for HDB's industrial property customers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Section 38 also provides for the transfer of the HDB officers currently serving the HDB customers to JTC.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: These officers will continue to serve existing HDB customers seamlessly as part of the JTC family.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: We have also placed emphasis on engaging the affected customers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Following our announcement of the transfer in 2016, HDB and JTC held several engagement sessions with the customers and their associations to hear and address their potential concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Many appreciated the greater convenience they would enjoy after the consolidation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Some HDB customers were concerned that rents may increase after the transfer.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: JTC has assured them that their contracted rents with HDB will continue for the current tenancies.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: In addition, HDB and JTC rents are largely similar.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: They are set based on similar principles and in line with market conditions.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The smooth transfer of the HDB officers is also a priority for us.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Section 39 of the Bill safeguards the officers' remuneration, leave rights and other terms of service.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: JTC has also conducted engagement sessions with the officers and designed an onboarding programme to familiarise them with JTC's work environment and to facilitate team building.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: HDB and JTC will continue to keep in close communication with the affected customers and officers in the lead-up to and after the transfer.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: This will minimise disruption to the transferred customers and ensure consistency and greater efficiency in JTC's treatment of customers across the consolidated property portfolio.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The third set of amendments is administrative in nature.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: It repeals Part IV of the JTC Act, which covers the sale and management of residential properties.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: These provisions were included in the JTC Act because of JTC's role in the 1970s and 1980s in building affordable flats and executive flats, largely for industrial workers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: All the affordable flats that JTC has built have been transferred to HDB, and the executive flats have been privatised and brought under the Land Titles (Strata) Act.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: Therefore, Part IV of the JTC Act is now obsolete.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: With these amendments to the JTC Act, the Town Councils Act will also be amended to remove the references to HDB's industrial properties.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Trade) (Mr Lim Hng Kiang)
text: The Housing and Development Act and the Residential Property Act will similarly be amended to delete references to Part IV of the JTC Act.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I do not object to the thrust of this Bill, and I support its enablement of the state to undertake more holistic master-planning of industrial estates across Singapore.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, I do have a few clarifications and suggestions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This was referred to in a speech by Minister Lim Hng Kiang on 19 October 2016.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If there are any disputes, will the Minister for Finance step in to determine the matter?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, on offences conducted under the Act, currently, section 64 requires that the consent of the Public Prosecutor is needed before any proceedings can be carried out against any person.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The reason for the repeal of this provision is not given.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I assume that, in this case, JTC lawyers can start proceedings on their own accord without the consent of the Public Prosecutor.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can the Minister confirm that and explain the rationale for that change?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Lastly, Mr Speaker, Sir, I would like to talk about the role of JTC in our economy in more broader terms.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In past debates in this House, the issue of the role of the state agencies − JTC and HDB − versus private developers in the market for industrial and commercial space has been discussed.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: JTC holds a far smaller share of industrial and commercial space than it did in the past.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Rental costs are not always the highest single component of the total cost structure facing SMEs and startups, though, in most cases, it is highly significant.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But equally importantly, they are the one element of the cost structure that we can control and change to perhaps a larger extent than any other.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In Singapore, the state owns most of the available land, something that is more or less unique among developed countries.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We need the SME sector to step up and do more of the heavy lifting in our economy in future to grow jobs and productivity and to become a thriving third pillar alongside multinational corporations (MNCs) and Government Linked Companies (GLCs).

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At the COS debate this year, my colleague Mr Dennis Tan highlighted how rental costs were "found to be the second factor with the greatest impact on profitability, coming in after manpower costs".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: He was referring to a survey that had recently been conducted, I believe, by the Singapore Business Federation (SBF).

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: He went on to say, "I hope the Government will consider conducting a major comprehensive historical and international benchmarking study on business rental costs to understand why rental costs rose so rapidly over the past two decades and why despite the Government's efforts in recent years to release more land through the Industrial Government Land Sales (IGLS) programme so as to ensure more industrial space, SMEs are still feeling the squeeze.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The study should also include how the cost of doing business in Singapore compares globally".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At the COS debate this year, I also pointed out how, even if business costs, such as rentals, have recently declined, in the absence of any confidence that such costs are going to be managed well in future, individuals may choose not to become entrepreneurs, since there is no degree of assurance that rentals will remain affordable in future, and no degree of assurance that a spike in rentals in future may push their business models into the zone of commercial non-viability.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Low cost today may not mean low cost tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At COS 2016, my colleague Mr Chen Show Mao said, "Over the longer term, access to low rent premises has diminished, following the corporatisation of JTC assets as well as the commercial pricing of HDB rentals.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We call on the Government to not only keep commercial and industrial rental increases near or below inflation but also to keep their absolute amounts manageable as part of the more serious effort to nurture SMEs as the third pillar.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This may require actions to, first, take a long-term view on reducing business rentals and have JTC pick up, in part, their former approach of building lower-cost industrial and commercial property, before many of their many properties were privatised".

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In his reply in 2016, Minister Lim had said, "the Government believes in letting market forces set the rent, and we allow the private sector to provide the responses in supplying the demand.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Where we intervene is where we recognise some possible market failures, for example, in startups where it is not so commercially viable to provide the space, the Government will step in, and, indeed, we have.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The downside of doing this is, of course, fiscal cost.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But it is not clear if the state providing lower-cost industrial and commercial space would stimulate entrepreneurship and value creation in such a way that the tax revenue from additional economic activity would partly or wholly offset the provision by the state of such low-cost land.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Moreover, keeping JTC's market share in the industrial and commercial market low while making ad hoc interventions to create pockets of low-cost space here and there also fails to address the concern that low cost today will not necessarily be low cost tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This target could be formed by considering the cost to the state of providing such land against the additional incremental revenue that the state would gain and the benefit to the economy and people of Singapore from the greater economic activity unleashed by such lower property costs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: At the risk of repetition, I make the observation here once again that the state owns most of the available land in Singapore and, hence, the Government has a unique responsibility to consider such issues and make such choices in a manner that benefits the whole society.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Attempting to control such costs through management of land supply to private developers is too blunt an instrument, given that there is never a perfect method of demand forecasting.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It could be argued that JTC providing low-cost rents would create excess demand and how then would we allocate the supply among competing companies?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A points-based balloting system is one mechanism to do so.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The principle behind such a system is reflected in other areas of public policy today, such as the allocation of school places.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It behooves the Government to think through these deeper and fundamental issues relating to the pricing of land for industrial and commercial use and to provide the necessary assurances to all stakeholders about its commitment to control costs now and in the future so as to unleash growth in SMEs and startups.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Speaker, after examining this Bill in detail, I support the JTC (Amendment) Bill.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Moving forward, all existing industrial tenants will be able to liaise with the same group of officers, assuring the tenants of service continuity.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: After consolidating all resources, JTC can be more effective in comprehensive planning for its industrial districts and integrating the whole value chain.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: At this time, I would also like to highlight three areas of concerns from businesses, and hope that the Minister and JTC could pay attention to them.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: HDB comes under the Ministry of National Development (MND) and is mainly responsible for public housing projects and creating a quality living environment for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The industrial properties and space provided by HDB also create employment opportunities close to home for many HDB residents.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: The relationship between many tenants and HDB is "Neighbours first, landlords second".

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: JTC, however, is a Statutory Board under MTI and is mainly responsible for developing industrial infrastructure facilities and promoting high value-added industrial development to propel the sustainable growth of Singapore's economy.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: In the first quarter of next year, factories in the heartlands will still remain, but the landlord would have changed; officers are the same, but they would have a different boss.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: JTC's land use is based on "economic benefits" and "economic value-add".

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Tenants are concerned that under the management of the new landlord, could the longtime practice of "discussion and reach a compromise" become negotiations purely based on "business considerations"?

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Everyone hopes that JTC could continue to be empathetic, offer a helping hand, and look after the ecosystem of the heartlands.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Before embarking on any major restructuring, we hope JTC could also carefully consider the indirect impact of the newly amended clauses, especially the impact on the livelihood of the employees of SMEs.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: However, after the lease terms are up, would JTC apply a different set of criteria to determine rentals?

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Would the renewal of rentals treat the above-mentioned "economic benefits" and "economic value-add" as a priority?

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Over the long term, demolishing and redeveloping factories are an inevitable trend.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Otherwise, it would be very difficult to realise the overall objective of "integrated planning".

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: However, many neighbourhood hawker centres see their rental and food prices go up after renovation.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Tenants are understandably worried that any renovation or redevelopment would cause rentals to soar.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: This would not only raise their overheads but also increase the cost of living for the public.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: Thirdly, how do the "small fish" co-exist with the "big fish"?

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: All along, HDB's industrial tenants have been SMEs, and are mostly family businesses in the traditional industries.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: On the other hand, many of JTC's tenants are medium to large manufacturers and MNCs.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: I have brought up in Parliament many times that policies cannot adopt "the one-size-fits-all" approach.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: We hope that JTC could make relevant decisions based on the needs of different customer groups.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: While evaluating and planning for the allocation of industrial land and factory space, besides considerations, such as the pace of industry growth and economic contributions, we do hope JTC could also consider the social functions of traditional industries.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: These enterprises are more willing to provide employment opportunities for older workers, which is a key factor in maintaining social stability.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: We could breathe new life into traditional industries.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: New opportunities will arise when we incorporate digital technology into traditional businesses.

speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
text: At the same time, I also appeal to the Government to provide substantive assistance to this group of tenants, helping small and micro enterprises to transform so that, in time to come, they could find a suitable space amongst JTC's many industrial properties.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: With this, JTC is now the "go to" agency when it comes to industrial property rental and resources and "know-how" on industrial properties while HDB can focus on the residential needs of the nation.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This move is very much applauded as it allows previous HDB industrial tenants to have access to more industrial properties and give them greater ability to do long-term planning.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: In the pursuit of restructuring the services rendered, it would be very much appreciated that much endeavour is taken to ensure that the affected employees are not worse off, with years of services being recognised and benefits being no less favourable.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: With reference to section 39(3), I would like to suggest disciplinary investigations and actions could be completed by HDB rather than brought over to JTC.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: This is to ensure that the employee starts with a clean slate with a new organisation.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Section 39 declares that a transfer as such will not give rise to any damages or compensation.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: To what extent was there consultation with the affected employees at HDB on their concerns of the transfer?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: The change in top management and organisation and issues, such as physical location of workplace and others, can impact the employee.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: If employees were not keen on the transfer to the new organisation, will they be given an option to redeploy the employee within HDB?

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: On the transfer of employees and their terms and conditions and issues pertaining to their transfer of employment, it is pertinent for the respective agencies of the affected staff to discuss the matter or had discussed the matter with the respective union or affected staff and give them ample time to arrive at a decision.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: A smooth and well thought through transfer will bring about greater staff morale and contentment.

speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
text: Pre- and post-employment transfer feedback from the affected staff should be addressed to ensure employees' operational efficiency.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These amendments were first announced last year and I understand that the discussion on consolidation has been going on between HDB and JTC for a few years now.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: JTC has done well over the past few decades to serve the needs of our business community.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As a strategic developer, some recent successes include the setting up of innovative spaces like JTC Launchpad, and strategic clustering of specialised spaces for industries, such as cleantech and biomedicals.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With a larger supply of industrial space in its arsenal, I believe it will be able to enhance its support for businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Businesses will also benefit administratively, as they would only need to contact one single agency to access public sector industrial facilities and spaces.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Tenants transferred under JTC will also find it easier to expand to adjacent spaces, as there will be options available.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can I also ask if there will be any other changes the tenants will face following the transfer to JTC?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is the Ministry able to share if there are plans to redevelop these properties, upon transfer to JTC, in order to maximise their plot ratio?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I understand that some of these older properties are low-rise, single-storey buildings occupying plots in prime locations.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Thirdly, some of the tenants are naturally concerned about JTC's divestment plans for the properties that will be transferred to them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many are aware that JTC had previously divested a portfolio of properties to a private trust sponsored by Mapletree.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: That said, I thank the Ministry for the much-awaited Bill as it streamlines our support for businesses, and I stand in support of it.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.40 pm.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.24 pm until 4.40 pm.
